clue.text: Revolutionary talk about a European tree or Atlantic inlet

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary, gives CHE

indicators.note: about means going round, so the talk word wraps the 'a'

parts.note: to talk is to speak
the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a radical speech touching on a European tree, set beside a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside SPEAK to give SAPEAK; 'or' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesapeake Bay is the large estuary on the US east coast opening onto the Atlantic Ocean.

clue.text: Church member is infiltrating movement unconsciously inspiring devotion

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so 'is' slips into the church-member letters

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a movement made unconsciously, read as A TIC

explanation.surface: A churchgoer secretly joins a movement and somehow inspires devotion without trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement unconsciously' is not a phrase about drifting into a church movement: it is two words read together as A TIC, an involuntary twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A charismatic leader has a compelling personal magnetism that draws devoted followers.

clue.text: Fix honour for boring press chief?

indicators.note: boring here means drilling into, so the honour sits inside the editor

parts.note: the chief of a newspaper is its editor, ED
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dull newspaper editor has rigged his own award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' is not 'dull' here but 'piercing', the container signal; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Having skill and directions, one should get the post

parts.note: address can mean dexterity or skill, as in handling a matter with address
E is the compass point east, used twice
E is the compass point east, used twice

explanation.surface: A capable person who knows the way surely deserves the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' gives two compass points, E and E; 'post' means mail, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom a letter or parcel is directed.

clue.text: Bribe raised to gag former king's betrayer

indicators.note: a gag fills a mouth, so the bribe goes inside the other letters

parts.note: ex means former
ER, Edward Rex, stands for a king

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sop is something offered to placate or bribe

explanation.surface: Money is paid to silence the man who sold out a deposed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' is the reversal signal of a down clue, and 'to gag' signals a container: a gag sits inside a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposer reveals someone's secrets, betraying them to public view.

clue.text: Solemn warning king's given over ex-orange-seller

indicators.note: in a down clue, given over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn sold oranges at Drury Lane before becoming Charles II's mistress

explanation.surface: A king hands a grave caution to a former fruit vendor.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was the orange-seller who became the mistress of King Charles II, a link the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the tolling of a bell, a portent of death or ending.

clue.text: Try to cheat in game held by brother officer?

indicators.note: held by means the cheating phrase sits inside the brother letters

parts.note: to rig a die is to load a dice to cheat in a game of chance

explanation.surface: A sibling in the services is suspected of fiddling at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' places RIG A DIE inside BR.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Variable in Paris and at the same time …

parts.note: Y is a mathematical variable
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A changeable French conjunction leads into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into 12 Down; it has no wordplay role.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet can mean nevertheless or simultaneously, as in 'strong yet gentle'.

clue.text: Sharp spike Sweeney Todd used without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the fictional demon barber of Fleet Street
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: The murderous barber uses a pointed blade without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the demon barber of Fleet Street in Victorian melodrama.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a backward-pointing spike, as on a fish-hook or arrow.

clue.text: Express disapproval of one held to lose value

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the one goes into the disapproval word

parts.note: to deprecate is to express disapproval of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on an individual detained for causing a fall in worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts I inside DEPRECATE; the clue's start is wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To depreciate is to fall in value over time, as a car does.

clue.text: Stupid, motorway still short of width

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the width letter is removed

parts.note: still air is windless

explanation.surface: A dull motorway, motionless and a bit narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is an adjective meaning calm, not 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means foolish, showing no thought or intelligence.

clue.text: Alliance giving the French the shivers

parts.note: le is French for the
ague is a fever marked by fits of shivering

explanation.surface: A coalition makes the French tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an association of states or groups united for a common purpose.

clue.text: … over in US, but curiously low-key

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The sentence from 7 Down runs on: and yet, over in America, oddly understated.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 7 Down for the surface only; 'curiously' rearranges the letters of OVER IN US BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unobtrusive means not conspicuous, quiet and restrained in manner.

clue.text: Opera manager takes a port after strike ends early

indicators.note: after means the trimmed strike word comes first
ends early means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: to impress is to strike or stamp, as a coin
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: The opera boss sets off for a harbour once a walkout ends ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends early' drops the last S of IMPRESS; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances concerts, plays or operas.

clue.text: When a sportsman's shot he's expected to make a recovery

definitions.text: When a sportsman's shot he's expected to make a recovery

parts.words: When a sportsman's shot he's expected to make a recovery
parts.note: reads like a wounded athlete recovering, but the shot is a game bird brought down, fetched by a gun dog

explanation.surface: A sportsman is shot and must recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is what the sportsman fired at, and 'recovery' is fetching it, not getting well.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog bred to bring back birds shot by hunters.

clue.text: Gregarious squadron leader's expenditure

parts.note: a gregarious person is outgoing and sociable

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sociable RAF squadron leader spends freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squadron leader' looks like an RAF rank, but it means the first letter of squadron.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are sums of money paid out, a household's spending.

clue.text: Smooth couple introducing Federation?

definitions.meaning: to press creases out of cloth
the first pair of letters of Federation are FE, the chemical symbol for the metal

explanation.surface: A suave pair launch a political union.
explanation.walkthrough: FE is the chemical symbol for iron, and it is the couple of letters that open Federation.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes flat with a hot appliance is to smooth them.

clue.text: Kids retreat, seeing animal on farm

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word for kids reads backwards

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: Children back away at the sight of a farm beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses TOTS; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stot is a dialect word for a young bullock or steer.

clue.text: Voters exultant about bully giving up heroin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the elated word wraps the bully

parts.note: elate is an old adjective meaning exultant, in high spirits

indicators.note: giving up means dropping, so the heroin letter goes

parts.note: to hector is to bully
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Delighted voters see a thug kick his drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' signals the drug letter dropped; 'about' signals a container. Elate is an old adjective, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote.

clue.text: Mournful English supporter's current account

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An English fan gives a sad account of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is electrical, symbol I, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the sorrowful tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Start of play about Jarndyce and Jarndyce, say

parts.note: Act I is the opening of a play
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A drama opens on the famous Chancery case.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarndyce and Jarndyce is the endless Chancery lawsuit in Dickens's Bleak House; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit, and the Dickens case is a famous one.

clue.text: Hospital in attractive position

indicators.note: in means the hospital letter goes inside the attractive word

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive

explanation.surface: A hospital sits in a pleasant spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a suitable place or role, a position that fits someone.

clue.text: Huge quarters a sleepy partygoer used endlessly

parts.note: E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass

indicators.note: endlessly means both ends are cut off

parts.note: the Dormouse dozes at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A drowsy reveller takes over vast lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips D and E from DORMOUSE to leave ORMOUS; 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large, immense.

clue.text: Communications knight expelled from Saudi city

indicators.note: expelled from means thrown out, so the knight letter goes

parts.note: Medina is a holy city in Saudi Arabia
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is thrown out of an Arabian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the means of mass communication: press, radio, television.

clue.text: Firm belief in being found guilty

definitions.meaning: the formal verdict of guilt in a court

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a settled certainty of mind and a guilty verdict in court.

clue.text: Disappointing start to race

explanation.definitionFit: The word means substandard and also, as a noun, the moment a race begins.

clue.text: Irish politicians giving duke trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Irish deputies make difficulties for a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil Éireann is Ireland's elected lower house, its body of deputies.

clue.text: To benefit Miss Pecksniff? Do me a favour!

definitions.meaning: Mercy Pecksniff is one of Mr Pecksniff's daughters in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, so doing something on her behalf is done for her

explanation.surface: Helping a Dickens character, or an exasperated cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of exasperation, like 'please' or 'give me a break'.
